newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan to meet on open skies next week - Slater.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan to meet on open skies next week - Slater.

text.p: Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater said Tuesday he will meet with his Japanese counterpart next week to discuss open skies proposals.

In a speech to the International Aviation Club, Slater said that pursuing open aviation markets was his top priority and repeated Washington's position that an agreement with Britain was a prerequisite for allowing the proposed alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines to go ahead.
Slater said he would meet with Japanese Transport Minister Makoto Koga next Monday in Canada during the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation ministerial meeting.
"I remain hopeful that, when we meet, Japan will decide to join with us in developing a plan to open our air market," he said.
Despite Japanese reticence, the United States continued to seek a fully liberalized open skies civil aviation regime with Japan in a "reasonable" time frame, he said.

He said that cargo services issues between the two countries needed to be resolved quickly in the context of broader bilateral talks. "But if not, it will be dealt with quickly on its own," Slater said.

On the negotiations with Britain, Slater told reporters that he hoped talks could resume "as soon as possible" after a lull because of the change in government in Britain and because of reviews on both sides of the Atlantic of the American Airlines/British Airways alliance.
Speaking on the proposed alliance, he said: "There is possibility. But there is no possibility without an open-skies agreement as a first step."
Antitrust immunity will require effective, competitive access for U.S. airlines at London's Heathrow airport, he said.
